# analytics-refresh-value

Value refresh on an analytics surface driven through its browser UI, parameterised per work item.

## When to invoke

A work item asks to refresh a value (a figure or short text) on an analytics surface whose only interface is a web UI. Preconditions:
- The target analytics surface is connected (listed in the Surfaces list with browser tools).
- The work item or its runbook names the approved source and the value to enter for this run.
- The runbook for that surface documents the page URL, the probe marker, the form element names and the read-back evidence.

## Inputs

Every value below is read from the current run's work item, its `Refs:` line, its `Reply target:` line, or the surface's runbook. None is a constant of this skill.

- `<record-id>` — the candidate's identifier on the surface the work came from (the `Refs:` line or the candidate id). Used to close the loop on the originating surface.
- `<requested-value>` — the figure or text the candidate or the runbook names for this run, taken from the approved source it cites. Enter it exactly; never calculate a replacement.
- `<reply-channel>` and `<reply-thread>` — from the `Reply target:` line when the work came from a chat channel or thread; used to post the completion note back into that thread.
- `<originating-surface>` — the slug of the surface the work came from. Its runbook says how the loop is closed there (an audit comment then a state change on a ticket; a reply in the thread on chat).
- `<audit-expectation>` — the read-back the runbook prescribes as evidence (an audit line, a returned identifier, a snapshot).
- `<analytics-surface>` — the slug of the connected analytics surface being refreshed, exactly as the Surfaces list names it.
- `<page-url>` — the page URL the analytics surface's runbook documents for the browser session.
- `<username-element>` — the login form's username field element name, from the runbook.
- `<password-element>` — the login form's password field element name, from the runbook.
- `<submit-element>` — the login submit element name, from the runbook.
- `<value-element>` — the single editable value field's element name, from the runbook.
- `<save-element>` — the save element name, from the runbook.
- `<target-state>` — the ticket state the originating surface's runbook prescribes after the refresh, when the originating surface is a ticket.
- `<login-username>` — the dashboard login username the runbook shows for this surface.

`{{secret}}` is the stored dashboard login credential for the analytics surface; it is substituted by the server and never written literally.

## Procedure

1. Read the runbook for the analytics surface. Confirm `<page-url>`, the probe marker, the form element names, and the evidence read-back. If any of these is missing, stop and record the gap.
2. Read the work item and identify `<requested-value>` from the approved source it names. Do not derive the value from any other system.
3. Open the documented page with `browser_navigate` on `<analytics-surface>`, targeting exactly `<page-url>`.
4. Take a `browser_snapshot` and confirm the probe marker. If the page shows a different origin or marker, record the observation and stop.
5. Fill the login form with `browser_fill_form`, using `<username-element>` and `<password-element>`, with `{{secret}}` as the password value.
6. Submit the login with `browser_click` on `<submit-element>`.
7. Fill the single editable value with `browser_fill_form` on `<value-element>`, value `<requested-value>` exactly.
8. Save with `browser_click` on `<save-element>`.
9. Take a `browser_snapshot` in the same session and read back `<audit-expectation>`. A successful click without that read-back is not evidence the change landed.
10. Close the loop on `<originating-surface>` per its runbook: on a ticket surface, emit a comment quoting the figure and the audit read-back, then a status change to `<target-state>` in the same response; on a chat surface, post the completion note to `<reply-channel>` / `<reply-thread>`.
11. If the page redirects, the login fails, an element is absent, or the audit read-back does not appear, record the observed failure as data, note it to the manager DM, and stop. Do not retry indefinitely or claim success.

## Actions emitted

The skill emits a typed `actions[]` array of real work-environment mutations. For a browser-driven analytics surface the writes are `mcp.call` actions against `<analytics-surface>`, using only the allowlisted browser tools and the probed argument names. Example shape (values are per-run inputs, not constants):

```json
[
  {"tool": "mcp.call", "surface": "<analytics-surface>", "tool": "browser_navigate", "toolArgsJson": "{\"url\":\"<page-url>\"}"},
  {"tool": "mcp.call", "surface": "<analytics-surface>", "tool": "browser_fill_form", "toolArgsJson": "{\"fields\":[{\"name\":\"<username-element>",\"value\":\"<login-username>\"},{\"name\":\"<password-element>",\"value\":\"{{secret}}\"}]}"},
  {"tool": "mcp.call", "surface": "<analytics-surface>", "tool": "browser_click", "toolArgsJson": "{\"element\":\"<submit-element>\"}"},
  {"tool": "mcp.call", "surface": "<analytics-surface>", "tool": "browser_fill_form", "toolArgsJson": "{\"fields\":[{\"name\":\"<value-element>",\"value\":\"<requested-value>\"}]}"},
  {"tool": "mcp.call", "surface": "<analytics-surface>", "tool": "browser_click", "toolArgsJson": "{\"element\":\"<save-element>\"}"},
  {"tool": "mcp.call", "surface": "<analytics-surface>", "tool": "browser_snapshot", "toolArgsJson": "{}"}
]
```

Closing the loop on a ticket surface emits, in the same response, a comment then a status change:

```json
[
  {"tool": "mcp.call", "surface": "<originating-surface>", "tool": "save_comment", "toolArgsJson": "{\"issue\":\"<record-id>\",\"body\":\"<completion note quoting the figure and the audit read-back>\"}"},
  {"tool": "mcp.call", "surface": "<originating-surface>", "tool": "save_issue", "toolArgsJson": "{\"id\":\"<record-id>\",\"state\":\"<target-state>\"}"}
]
```

On a chat surface the completion note is an `http.request` POST `chat.postMessage` with `channel` set to `<reply-channel>` and `thread_ts` set to `<reply-thread>`. Never copy a public reply draft into the manager DM; the DM carries at most a one-line note of what was done.

## Verification

- The `browser_snapshot` after save shows `<audit-expectation>` (for example, the audit line beneath the tile) and the visible `<requested-value>`.
- The completion note on `<originating-surface>` quotes both the figure and the audit read-back.
- No screenshot, code evaluation, file upload, arbitrary tab, or navigation to another origin appears in the actions.
- `{{secret}}` appears only inside the login `browser_fill_form` payload, never in a comment, message, or note.

# chat-thread-reply

Post a threaded reply on a chat surface, closing the loop on a request that arrived in a channel or thread. Every value that varies per run comes from that run's work item and the surface runbook; nothing here is a constant for one team or channel.

## When to invoke

Invoke when the work item is a chat-surface request that must be answered in the thread it came from: the candidate names a chat message (or thread) as its source, and the runbook for the originating surface prescribes a reply in that thread as the way the loop is closed. Preconditions:

- The originating surface is a connected chat surface (see the run's Surfaces list). If no connected surface exists for it, emit no action and record that in `notes`.
- The candidate carries a `Reply target:` line giving the source channel and thread timestamp.
- The reply text is known for this run: it is `<requested-value>`, taken from the candidate or the runbook, never invented here.

## Inputs

- `<record-id>` — the candidate's identifier on the surface the work came from (the `Refs:` line or the candidate id). Preserved in the reply text so the thread stays traceable.
- `<requested-value>` — the figure or text the candidate or the runbook names for this run; the substance of the reply.
- `<reply-channel>` — the source channel id from the `Reply target:` line.
- `<reply-thread>` — the source thread timestamp from the `Reply target:` line.
- `<originating-surface>` — the slug of the surface the work came from, named exactly as the Surfaces list names it. Its runbook says how the loop is closed there (a reply in the thread on chat; an audit comment then a state change on a ticket elsewhere).
- `<audit-expectation>` — the read-back the runbook prescribes as evidence (a provider timestamp, a returned message identifier, an audit line).

## Procedure

1. Read the candidate and its `Reply target:` line. Confirm `<reply-channel>` and `<reply-thread>` are present. If either is missing, do not guess a channel id or timestamp: emit no action and raise the gap in the manager DM as a question.
2. Read the runbook for `<originating-surface>`. Confirm it prescribes a threaded reply (`chat.postMessage` with `channel` plus `thread_ts`) as the loop-closing step. If it prescribes something else for this surface, that is a different skill's job; stop.
3. Compose the reply text for this run from `<requested-value>`, preserving `<record-id>` in the text so the thread keeps its trace to the source record. One logical message, no provenance trailer, no `username` or `icon_emoji` override: the server appends the employee name and run id.
4. Emit the reply as its own action (see below). Write the text exactly as it should land; the executor decides, from the current run mode, whether it is sent as emitted or held for the manager's approval of the exact text. Never state approval-state language in the message itself.
5. Do not copy the reply draft anywhere else. The manager DM carries only questions, escalation, or a one-line note of what was done — never the reply text that belongs in the channel.
6. Read back against `<audit-expectation>`: confirm the action's shape matches the runbook (surface slug, path, channel, thread timestamp) and record the returned evidence (for example a provider timestamp) in the run notes.

## Actions emitted

Exactly one real-surface action per reply, an `http.request` POST to `chat.postMessage` on the originating chat surface:

```json
{
  "tool": "http.request",
  "args": {
    "surface": "<originating-surface>",
    "method": "POST",
    "path": "/chat.postMessage",
    "headersJson": "{\"Authorization\":\"Bearer {{secret}}\",\"Content-Type\":\"application/json; charset=utf-8\"}",
    "body": "{\"channel\":\"<reply-channel>\",\"thread_ts\":\"<reply-thread>\",\"text\":\"<requested-value> (ref <record-id>)\"}"
  }
}
```

- `surface` must match the Surfaces list slug exactly; only a connected surface may be targeted.
- `channel` is `<reply-channel>` from the `Reply target:` line, never a display name or a guessed id.
- `thread_ts` is `<reply-thread>`; omit it only if the runbook for this run says the reply is a channel-level post rather than a thread reply.
- `{{secret}}` is written literally; the server substitutes the stored credential. Never include a token or key.
- A skill that produces only prose with no actions is broken: if the reply cannot be emitted (missing reply target, unconnected surface), emit no action and say why in `notes`.

## Verification

The executor reads back, per run:

- One `http.request` action targeting `<originating-surface>` with path `/chat.postMessage`.
- The body's `channel` equals `<reply-channel>` and `thread_ts` equals `<reply-thread>` from the `Reply target:` line.
- The body's `text` carries `<requested-value>` and preserves `<record-id>`.
- Headers carry `Authorization: Bearer {{secret}}` with no literal token.
- The run notes record the evidence `<audit-expectation>` prescribes (for example the provider timestamp returned for the post).
- No reply draft appears in the manager DM; the DM, if used at all, holds only a question, escalation, or a one-line note of what was done.

# kanban-comment-and-close

Add an audit comment to a ticket on a kanban work-management surface, then change the ticket's state — in that order, in the same response. Each run's values come from the work item and its runbook; nothing is hardcoded.

## When to invoke

Invoke when a work item asks for a comment (audit note, close summary, status explanation) to be written on a ticket in a kanban system, optionally followed by a state change on that same ticket. Preconditions:

- The work names a ticket on a connected kanban surface (for example `linear`).
- The runbook for that surface documents a comment tool and an issue-update tool, and the surface's allowlist contains them.
- The requested comment text or figure is supplied by the candidate or the runbook for this run.

If the surface is not connected, emit no actions and say so in `notes`.

## Inputs

- `<record-id>` — the ticket's identifier on the originating surface, read from the candidate's `Refs:` line or the candidate id (e.g. the issue identifier or provider id).
- `<requested-value>` — the figure or text the candidate or the runbook names for this run: the comment body content, and, when a state change is requested, the exact workflow-state name to move the ticket to. Never a constant in this skill.
- `<reply-channel>` and `<reply-thread>` — the `Reply target:` line when the work came from a chat channel or thread; used only to close the loop there.
- `<originating-surface>` — the slug of the surface the work came from, exactly as the Surfaces list names it; its runbook says how the loop is closed there (audit comment then state change on a ticket; a reply in the thread on chat).
- `<audit-expectation>` — the read-back the runbook prescribes as evidence (an audit line, a returned comment identifier, a snapshot of the ticket state).

## Procedure

1. Read the candidate and the runbook for `<originating-surface>`. Confirm the ticket identifier `<record-id>`, the requested comment content and, if requested, the target state name from `<requested-value>`. Never invent an identifier, state name or result.
2. Optionally read the ticket back from the surface (e.g. `get_issue` with `id` set to `<record-id>`) to confirm it exists and to discover the workspace's exact workflow-state names before writing.
3. Emit the comment action first. For a kanban surface reached over MCP, this is one `mcp.call` with `surface` set to `<originating-surface>`, `tool` set to the runbook's comment tool (e.g. `save_comment`), and `toolArgsJson` carrying the ticket identifier and the comment body — for Linear, `{"issueId":"<record-id>","body":"<requested-value>"}`. Send only the fields the runbook names; never send a comment id or parent id, which would rewrite or reply. One action per comment.
4. If the requested effect is complete and a state change is requested, emit the state-change action in the same response, after the comment. For Linear this is one `mcp.call` with `tool` set to `save_issue` and `toolArgsJson` `{"id":"<record-id>","state":"<requested-value>"}`. A status change must never be the only trace of who acted, and must always be preceded in the same response by the comment. A partial result gets a comment and stays in progress — no state change.
5. Do not change assignee, priority, labels or description unless the approved action for this run lists it.
6. If the work came from a chat channel or thread, close the loop there: emit an `http.request` POST to `chat.postMessage` with `channel` set to `<reply-channel>` and `thread_ts` set to `<reply-thread>`, body a one-line note of what was done. Never copy a public reply draft into the manager DM; the manager DM carries only a one-line note of what was done.
7. Do not add a provenance trailer or a `username` to any comment or message: the server appends the employee name and run id. Write `{{secret}}` where the runbook shows the credential, and never include a token or key value.
8. At execution time, read the current action mode from the run context and describe effects accordingly; never hardcode approval-state language into comments or messages.

## Actions emitted

Every run ends with a typed `actions[]` array. Example shapes (values are per-run inputs, not constants):

```json
[
  {"tool": "mcp.call", "args": {"surface": "<originating-surface>", "tool": "save_comment", "toolArgsJson": "{\"issueId\":\"<record-id>\",\"body\":\"<requested-value>\"}"}},
  {"tool": "mcp.call", "args": {"surface": "<originating-surface>", "tool": "save_issue", "toolArgsJson": "{\"id\":\"<record-id>\",\"state\":\"<requested-value>\"}"}}
]
```

A chat-sourced run adds a third action:

```json
{"tool": "http.request", "args": {"surface": "slack", "method": "POST", "path": "chat.postMessage", "headersJson": "{\"Authorization\": \"Bearer {{secret}}\", \"Content-Type\": \"application/json; charset=utf-8\"}", "body": "{\"channel\":\"<reply-channel>\",\"thread_ts\":\"<reply-thread>\",\"text\":\"<one-line note of what was done>\"}"}}
```

A skill that produces only prose with no actions is broken.

## Verification

Read back against `<audit-expectation>` from the runbook:

- The comment tool's response returns a comment identifier (or the audit line the runbook prescribes); confirm it names `<record-id>`.
- If a state change was emitted, read the ticket back (e.g. `get_issue` with `id` set to `<record-id>`) and confirm it reports the requested state.
- Confirm the actions appeared in the order: comment, then state change.
- If the work came from chat, confirm the thread note posted to `<reply-channel>`/`<reply-thread>`.
- If any read-back fails, comment on the ticket with the observed result and leave the state unchanged; report the discrepancy in `notes`.

# SKILL: see-internal-docs

## When to invoke
The boss or a teammate has asked a question whose answer is plausibly in the team's internal docs (wiki pages, runbooks, onboarding material).

## Inputs
- `query` (string): the question or topic to look up.
- `docs_index` (array of {title, body}): the searchable internal-docs corpus exposed by Day0's docs surface.

## Procedure
1. Tokenise the query; identify 2-4 key terms (proper nouns, domain words, action verbs).
2. Score each doc by token overlap with title (weight 3) + body (weight 1).
3. Take the top 3 docs, read them in full.
4. Synthesise an answer in 2-4 sentences. Cite each fact back to its doc title in parentheses.
5. If the docs do not answer the question, say so explicitly. Do not invent.

## Output
- `answer` (string): the synthesised answer with inline citations.
- `docs_consulted` (array of strings): titles of docs read.
- `coverage` ("complete" | "partial" | "none"): your confidence the docs covered the question.

## Boundaries
- Drafts only — never claim an answer was posted to the team.
- If the question implies needing to *change* something (update a spreadsheet, file a ticket), surface that as a follow-up; this skill is read-only.
